title: The agentic web is here
gist: MIT Technology Review argues the 'agentic web' of LLM agents (Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots, Anthropic's Claude Duet) has arrived earlier than expected, via both connectors/tools and computer-use agents (GPT-6 Astra 73% on OSWorld 2.0), and it threatens the attention-economy business model of publishers and e-commerce. The open question is whether it decentralizes power or consolidates it into platform-controlled walled gardens, with incumbents like Amazon already blocking rival agents.

insights.claim: Autonomous software agents that use the internet for people, envisioned by Tim Berners-Lee's 2001 Semantic Web, have now been realized via tools such as Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet, which are given access to email inboxes and bank accounts.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Agents with financial and communications access create a new consumer-interface layer.
